answer:
Build a 2D lid-driven cavity flow case for OpenFOAM using the icoFoam incompressible solver.
The domain is a square cavity of 0.1 m by 0.1 m, extruded 0.01 m in the z-direction for 2D simulation.
Create a uniform blockMesh of 20 cells by 20 cells in x-y and 1 cell in z, giving cell size 0.005 m by 0.005 m.
The eight block vertices are (0 0 0), (0.1 0 0), (0.1 0.1 0), (0 0.1 0) and their z-offset counterparts at z=0.01.
Define four boundary patches: movingWall on the top face (y=0.1), fixedWalls on the left, right, and bottom faces, and frontAndBack on the two z-faces.
Set frontAndBack patches to empty type.
Set movingWall to no-slip wall with velocity fixedValue uniform (1 0 0).
Set fixedWalls to no-slip wall with velocity fixedValue uniform (0 0 0).
Use kinematic viscosity nu = 0.001 m2/s in constant/transportProperties, yielding Reynolds number Re = 100 (laminar).
Do NOT use any turbulence model; run purely laminar icoFoam.
In system/controlDict set startTime 0, endTime 0.5, deltaT 0.002, writeControl timeStep, writeInterval 20.
Do NOT enable adjustTimeStep, maxCo, or any adaptive time-stepping mechanism.
The simulation runs exactly 250 time steps and writes approximately 13 output directories (at t = 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, ... up to 0.5 s plus the initial time).
Set initial velocity field to uniform (0 0 0) and initial pressure to uniform 0.
Generate all required case files (blockMeshDict, transportProperties, 0/U, 0/p, controlDict, fvSchemes, fvSolution) so the case runs with blockMesh followed by icoFoam without further editing.
